evidence_items.relevant_text: The Eyalet of Cyprus (Ottoman Turkish: ایالت قبرص, Eyālet-i Ḳıbrıṣ)[1] was an eyalet/province of the Ottoman Empire made up of the island of Cyprus, which was annexed into the Empire in 1571.[2] The Ottomans changed the way they administered Cyprus multiple times. It was a sanjak/sub-province (… ) of the Eyalet of the Archipelago from 1670 to 1703, and again from 1784 to 1914; a fief of the Grand Vizier (1703–1745 and 1748–1784); and again an eyalet for the short period from 1745 to 1748.[3]
evidence_items.summary: The page states directly that Cyprus was a “fief of the Grand Vizier” during two intervals: 1703–1745 and 1748–1784, with a brief eyalet period from 1745–1748.
